blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, individual transactions are not merely accounting entries — they are signals about how the business is actually behaving. A pattern of small, unusual refunds tells a story about a product that is quietly disappointing customers. A spike in credit notes says something about quality or communication. A category of expenses that only ever gets approved at the last minute reveals a decision process that is breaking somewhere upstream.

Senior finance leaders learn to notice these patterns the way a doctor notices small symptoms. Individually, each one is unimportant. In combination, they reveal things that the P&L will eventually confirm — usually too late to act calmly.

The signals are almost always in the detail. The senior skill is staying close enough to the detail to hear them, while staying far enough away from it to see the pattern.

items.q: According to the text, what are individual transactions at senior level?
options: Signals about how the business is behaving
items.why: "they are signals about how the business is actually behaving" — vão além do lançamento contábil.

items.q: What does a category of expenses approved only at the last minute reveal?
options: A decision process breaking somewhere upstream
items.why: "reveals a decision process that is breaking somewhere upstream."

items.q: Why does the text compare senior finance leaders to a doctor?
options: Because both rely on standardised procedures
Because both must act with formal authority
Because both work under regulatory scrutiny
Because both read small symptoms that matter only in combination
items.why: "notice these patterns the way a doctor notices small symptoms… In combination, they reveal things."

items.q: The phrase "usually too late to act calmly" most strongly suggests that…
options: the P&L is an unreliable document
calm is impossible in senior finance roles
transactions should never be reviewed individually
waiting for the P&L to confirm a problem forces a reactive, pressured response
items.why: Inferência: quando o P&L confirma, já é tarde — daí a vantagem de ler os sinais antes.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The P&L is the earliest reliable warning of trouble.
Staying too close to the detail can obscure the pattern.
Small anomalies can foreshadow larger problems.
Detail and pattern must be held in tension.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo defende que os sinais precedem o P&L, que confirma tarde demais.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver revisando os dados de transações. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So I've now been through three months of transaction data line by line, and I want to walk you through what I found — because it started as almost nothing.

It began with a handful of credit notes. Six, maybe seven, all small, all issued to different customers, all in the same product family. Individually, not one of them would have flagged anything. No single number was large enough to breach a threshold or trip an alert. But sitting side by side, they had a shape. They were telling the same story from slightly different angles.

When I pulled the underlying orders, the pattern held. Same batch window, same complaint dressed up in different words — a finish that wasn't quite right. Nobody had raised it formally. It never reached a quality report. It simply leaked out through the finance ledger as a scatter of tiny reversals.

Here's my worry. If I'd waited for this to show up in the P&L, we would have been reading about it as a margin problem, under pressure, with the customer already gone. Instead we caught it as a whisper. My recommendation is that we treat these small reversals as an early-warning feed, not as noise to be cleaned up at month end.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How did the problem first appear in the data?
options: As a single large credit note
As a sudden drop in margin
As a handful of small credit notes across the same product family
items.why: "a handful of credit notes… all small… all in the same product family."

items.q: Why did none of the credit notes trigger an alert on their own?
options: No single number was large enough to breach a threshold
They were filed under the wrong account
They were issued to the same customer
items.why: "No single number was large enough to breach a threshold or trip an alert."

items.q: What did Oliver find when he pulled the underlying orders?
options: A pricing error in the ledger
The same batch window and the same complaint in different words
That the notes had been duplicated
items.why: "Same batch window, same complaint dressed up in different words."

items.q: When Oliver says the problem "leaked out through the finance ledger," he implies that…
options: the finance team caused the quality issue
the ledger caught what the formal quality process missed
items.why: Inferência: o problema nunca virou relatório de qualidade; apareceu primeiro no razão financeiro.

items.q: What is Oliver's core recommendation?
options: Escalate every credit note to the board
Wait for the P&L to confirm the margin impact
Treat small reversals as an early-warning feed rather than noise
Clean up the small reversals at month end
items.why: "treat these small reversals as an early-warning feed, not as noise to be cleaned up at month end."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Read the ledger for what each entry is telling you." In this context, a signal is…
items.why: Signal = sinal: uma indicação do que está realmente acontecendo por baixo dos números.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A scatter of small ___ issued to different customers pointed to a single faulty batch."
items.why: Refunds = reembolsos: pequenos reembolsos que, somados, revelaram o lote defeituoso.

items.q: "The decision was breaking somewhere upstream." Upstream here means…
options: earlier in the process, before finance sees it
items.why: Upstream = a montante: mais cedo no fluxo, antes de o problema chegar às finanças.

items.q: "Each anomaly is a symptom, not the disease." A symptom is…
options: a visible sign that points to a deeper problem
items.why: Symptom = sintoma: o sinal visível de uma causa mais profunda.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Expenses that only ever get signed at the ___ suggest a broken approval process."
items.why: Last minute = última hora: aprovar sempre em cima da hora revela um processo quebrado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre dados financeiros. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on each credit note above the limit." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's drill down into the underlying orders before we conclude anything." To drill down into means to…
items.why: Drill down into = descer ao detalhe, analisar granularmente.

items.q: "Two of these small reversals flag up a quality issue nobody reported." To flag up means to…
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo.

items.q: "We can't just write off the pattern as noise." To write off here means to…
items.why: Write off = descartar como irrelevante (também 'baixar' um valor incobrável).

items.q: "Caught early, a whisper like this won't snowball into a margin crisis." To snowball into means to…
options: grow rapidly into something much larger
items.why: Snowball into = crescer descontroladamente até virar algo bem maior.
